transcript.text: AEG IKB64301FB induction hob keeps beeping and showing Er03 then switches off. Pan of pasta boiled over just before.

The 'Er03' code isn't in my standard database for AEG hobs, but given that a pan boiled over immediately before this happened, the most likely cause is that the spillage caused an overheating event or moisture ingress into the controls. Induction hobs have safety sensors that trigger a shutdown and error if they detect excessive heat or electrical faults from liquid intrusion. Please do the following checks:
1. Isolate the hob: Switch it off at the wall (via the fused spur or consumer unit) to ensure it is completely safe and powered down.
2. Check for moisture: Look underneath the hob (if accessible) and around the control panel area for any signs of pasta water or dampness. If you see liquid, leave it isolated and dry for 24-48 hours in a warm, dry room before trying again.
3. Listen for the fan: When you turn it back on (after ensuring it is dry), listen carefully near the hob for the cooling fan running. A healthy hob should have a faint whirring sound when active. If the hob remains damp after drying, or if the error returns immediately even with no pans on it, this points to a failed component like the cooling fan or the main PCB needing engineer attention.
Switched it off at the wall for 5 mins after wiping it dry (there was starchy water across the slider) and it works now, all four zones fine. Is that ok, or should I do something else?

That is perfectly fine. The error was the hob's safety system reacting to the spillage and potential moisture or heat buildup; once you isolated it and wiped it dry, the sensors reset and everything returned to normal. To stop this from happening again, just try to keep an eye on boiling pans and wipe up any spills as soon as they cool down enough to touch. If it happens again despite keeping things clean and dry, then we would need to look at internal components, but for now you are good to go.

candidates: Cooling fan failure or blocked ventilation (medium)
Main PCB fault due to moisture ingress (low)

reading.symptom: keeps beeping and showing Er03 then switches off

plan: Already given by the customer, never ask for it again: make AEG; model IKB64301FB; code ER03.
The fault they reported is: "keeps beeping and showing Er03 then switches off". Keep to it: never describe a symptom, result or state they have not told you.

Stage 1 (broad help): say what could cause this, most likely first, as possibilities rather than certainties, including simple causes (settings, loading, detergent, installation, or normal behaviour) where they fit. Then give the safe checks that best tell those causes apart (most useful and simplest first, usually two to four), each with why it helps and what each result would mean; or, if one question would settle it sooner, ask that. Do not ask for the model number in this reply. Do not tell them to buy, order or replace a part yet.

Explain what the error code means using ERROR CODES. If ERROR CODES does not resolve it, say plainly that you cannot confirm what it means on their model (it may not be an error code at all, for example part of the model name), never guess a meaning, and work from the symptoms.
They asked: "Is that ok, or should I do something else?" - answer that first.
The customer says it is fixed: say so warmly, give one short tip to stop it happening again, and ask if there is anything else.
